title: Uncertainty-Aware World Model for Aerial Image-Goal Navigation
review_scope: Methods, experiments and stated limitations on listed pages; figure-only pages are not counted as visually inspected unless separately recorded.
review: AUTHOR METHOD: A frozen DINOv3 feature world model predicts action-conditioned futures. A separately trained Hierarchical Error Projection head explains residuals through multiscale low-rank subspaces; candidate goals are scored by unexplained residual energy. This is structured error scoring, not calibrated failure probability. PAPER EXPERIMENT: The matched deterministic backbone improves aerial planning; AirSim uses a 20 m goal tolerance and the physical pilot five tasks. Supplement G requires strong anisotropy to motivate ignoring parallel residuals; greedy projections are not a general exact global projection. INSPECTED CODE: normalized training averages patchwise ratios rather than the paper's ratio of summed energies. Optional parallel-residual weighting and same-goal wrong-action contrastive losses already exist, although disabled by default. DEDUCTION: a new decision-aligned objective must compare these controls. Construction M3 below demonstrates a possible lost task direction, not trained-model failure.
limitations: No benchmark run; deployment wrappers downloaded but not deeply inspected; scene-disjoint AirGoal split not established; final qualitative figures not visually audited.

title: CPNAV: Calibrated Vision-Language Navigation for Object-Goal Search in Unseen Environments
venue_or_status: Preprint on official author publications page
review_scope: Methods, experiments and stated limitations on listed pages; figure-only pages are not counted as visually inspected unless separately recorded.
review: AUTHOR METHOD: Offline oracle search optimizes the minimum semantic score along a successful path; an episode-score quantile retains admissible actions for depth-first backtracking. Its stated exchangeability condition concerns complete episodes. PAPER/REPORTING: The text also describes independent observation/action calibration scenarios; the calibration unit, threshold complements and sample counts need reconciliation. Eq 12 uses the .99 upper Beta quantile while claiming 99% confidence, then says confidence 1−δ. The visually checked formula does not support the claimed confidence interpretation (M1). Oracle-path retention alone also does not ensure budgeted success (M5). Target visibility judged manually differs from standard distance-based ObjectNav. The linked official repository was inaccessible. DEDUCTION: do not present its score threshold as a certified collision-risk controller.
limitations: Repository not found at retrieval, not proof no code exists; no raw calibration scores; no benchmark executed.

title: Adaptive Rollout Truncation Based on Epistemic Uncertainty for Efficient Offline World Model Training
venue_or_status: Accepted IROS 2026 workshop, author-reported; not main conference
review_scope: Methods, experiments and stated limitations on listed pages; figure-only pages are not counted as visually inspected unless separately recorded.
review: AUTHOR METHOD: A GRU world model with bootstrap heads or dropout truncates training rollouts when epistemic disagreement crosses a warm-up threshold, bounded between four and 32 steps. PAPER EXPERIMENT: ANYmal/Ant offline prediction and rollout-compute results support efficiency in that training setting. Appendix F explicitly finds that replaying the induced horizon schedule without uncertainty gating matches within seed noise; it disclaims coverage calibration. Appendix C reports no clear downstream MOPO-PPO advantage. DEDUCTION: adaptive horizon proposals require a matched schedule replay control, and prediction efficiency is insufficient evidence for better navigation decisions. No official implementation of this new truncation method was verified; the cited predecessor repository is not substituted for it.
limitations: No new-method source inspection; no deployment experiment reproduced.

title: Policy-Guided World Model Planning for Language-Conditioned Visual Navigation
review_scope: Methods, experiments and stated limitations on listed pages; figure-only pages are not counted as visually inspected unless separately recorded.
review: AUTHOR METHOD: Language-conditioned Octo proposals initialize MPPI; an action-conditioned JEPA scores terminal image-feature proximity. Training uses frozen image encoders and latent prediction. PAPER EXPERIMENT: CAST validation ATE/RPE are offline trajectory comparisons; proposal scoring nearly matches iterative optimization for several metrics. Closed-loop validation remains future work. INSPECTED CODE: eval_octo_mppi_cast.py:670-703 explicitly takes the recorded final frame as goal. Its defaults differ from the paper's candidate/elite/temperature settings; training defaults to one-step loss and optional rollout losses detach previous predictions. No live controller is evaluated by this script. DEDUCTION: report image-goal access and reranking compute separately when transferring this mechanism to instruction-only VLN.
limitations: No fetched code execution; full Octo training/data pipeline not audited; no checkpoint download.

title: WorldMAP: Bootstrapping Vision-Language Navigation Trajectory Prediction with Generative World Models
review_scope: Methods, experiments and stated limitations on listed pages; figure-only pages are not counted as visually inspected unless separately recorded.
review: AUTHOR METHOD: Generated future views, depth/pose reconstruction, language-guided segmentation and BEV/FMM planning produce teacher trajectories. A Qwen3-VL-based multihypothesis student distills these offline. PAPER EXPERIMENT: Target-Bench uses trajectories projected onto the initial image and pixel-space ADE/FDE/DTW. Pseudo-label-only ADE is 95.98 versus 78.34 for ground truth and 42.06 combined (Table III); gains therefore involve mixed supervision. Training-free direct VLM comparisons also change architecture and data. Appendix B's inference description invokes best-of-K without fully specifying confidence training/selection. DEDUCTION: projected path accuracy does not establish collision-free physical execution or online forecast reliability. No official code located in bounded title/author searches.
limitations: No implementation inspection; no actual closed-loop execution evaluated in reviewed evidence; qualitative figures not visually interpreted.

title: JanusVLN: Decoupling Semantics and Spatiality with Dual Implicit Memory for Vision-Language Navigation
review_scope: Methods, experiments and stated limitations on listed pages; figure-only pages are not counted as visually inspected unless separately recorded.
review: AUTHOR METHOD: RGB-only Qwen2.5-VL combines semantic features with frozen VGGT geometry and bounded initial/recent memory. Training includes extra ScaleVLN and DAgger trajectories. PAPER EXPERIMENT: Geometry/cache ablations support the tested architecture; Appendix D acknowledges recovery and premature stopping failures. INSPECTED CODE: VGGT caches first 8/recent 48 frames. Released evaluation instead resamples up to eight historical RGB images over the whole episode and calls the language model afresh; persistent semantic/LLM caches claimed in the paper were not found on that path. DEDUCTION: old observations are neither universally retained nor universally absent after 48 frames. Memory comparisons must specify raw-frame storage, sampling and geometric cache separately.
limitations: No benchmark run; complete optimizer/preprocessing not audited; source path may differ from paper experiments.

title: HumanoidVLN: A Physics-Grounded Simulator and Benchmark for Vision-Language Navigation Across Diverse Humanoid Embodiments
venue_or_status: arXiv preprint; project says Humanoids 2026 under review
review_scope: Methods, experiments and stated limitations on listed pages; figure-only pages are not counted as visually inspected unless separately recorded.
review: AUTHOR METHOD: Physics-based humanoid execution combines morphology-specific RL locomotion with PD/MPC tracking and curated large navigable scenes. All 933 episodes form one zero-shot evaluation set. PAPER EXPERIMENT: Fall rates vary substantially by robot/model; action interface, tracker and locomotion policy vary together. The 20-pair real/sim pilot uses one checkpoint and two scenes, explicitly not scene-level generalization. DEDUCTION: the suite makes physical failures measurable, but does not identify an architecture-only cause or solve them. Scene filtering excludes tight environments. Code/data are promised on acceptance, limiting immediate independent replication.
limitations: No available code/dataset inspection; no robot execution.

title: ReInsVLN: Revisiting Historical Evidence for Training-Free Vision-and-Language Navigation
review_scope: Methods, experiments and stated limitations on listed pages; figure-only pages are not counted as visually inspected unless separately recorded.
review: AUTHOR METHOD: ReInsBench freezes failed navigator checkpoints; deployment combines fixed-history revisits and instruction-aware visual-token compression. PAPER EXPERIMENT: R0 versus neutral reminders improves 19/812 branches, 2.34 pp, with trajectory-cluster 95% CI [-0.99, 5.68]. Diagnostic checkpoint/suffix construction uses reference actions; deployed fixed reminders at steps 2/13 use the original instruction. Seven of 11 pilot net gains already occur at initial registration. FHR also breaks 78/71 previously successful Stream/Intern episodes while recovering 173/126. DEDUCTION: the diagnostic does not isolate restoration of lost history from improved initial grounding; deployment efficacy and explanatory attribution are separate. Its small real-world ordinal comparison changes doorway conditions. Reuse of historical evidence alone is established prior art.
limitations: Official implementation/supplement not found in bounded search; full eight-page paper reviewed; no experiments reproduced.

title: DART-VLN: Test-Time Memory Decay and Anti-Loop Regularization for Discrete Vision-Language Navigation
review_scope: Methods, experiments and stated limitations on listed pages; figure-only pages are not counted as visually inspected unless separately recorded.
review: AUTHOR METHOD: Frozen GridMM receives read-side age/repetition/novelty weighting and finite next-hop reversal/revisit penalties. PAPER EXPERIMENT: Same-checkpoint R2R/REVERIE comparisons improve several metrics; endpoint error is not uniformly improved. INSPECTED CODE: weights enter as log-priors in per-cell softmax; anti-loop penalties subtract from probabilities, with STOP unchanged. No memory-slot pruning occurs in that aggregation path. DEDUCTION: equal floored priors cancel exactly (M4), so this does not erase all stale evidence. Runtime reduction is an empirical report, not a consequence proved by reweighting alone. Finite penalties preserve the possibility of necessary backtracking but can still discourage it.
limitations: No fetched code execution; full environment metadata update not audited.

title: CMMR-VLN: Vision-and-Language Navigation via Continual Multimodal Memory Retrieval
review_scope: Methods, experiments and stated limitations on listed pages; figure-only pages are not counted as visually inspected unless separately recorded.
review: AUTHOR METHOD: Viewpoint-indexed image/landmark memory retrieves prior experience as high-priority navigation rules; successful routes and first erroneous failure steps update memory. PAPER EXPERIMENT: R2R and 20 physical instructions support gains under this experience-augmented protocol. However the source of first-error labels, initial memory access, episode ordering and learned attention matrix training are not sufficiently specified for a fully label-free interpretation. Ablations use a different subset from main results. DEDUCTION: outcome-aware retrieval is prior art, but changing memory/feedback contracts prevents attributing its gains purely to a retrieval mechanism. No official implementation verified in the bounded search.
limitations: Feedback provenance and attention training unresolved; no source code inspected.

title: ImagineNav++: Prompting Vision-Language Models as Embodied Navigator through Scene Imagination
venue_or_status: Journal-style arXiv preprint; venue acceptance not independently verified
review_scope: Methods, experiments and stated limitations on listed pages; figure-only pages are not counted as visually inspected unless separately recorded.
review: AUTHOR METHOD: A trained Where2Imagine module predicts waypoints; novel-view synthesis supplies candidate images to a frozen VLM, followed by learned VER PointNav. DINOv2-based hierarchical keyframes retain denser recent history. PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table V's full-history control does not improve success; selected history improves efficiency/quality, with an incremental approximation tradeoff. Table I distinguishes generated-future HM3D 58.5/26.6 SR/SPL from oracle-real-future 62.5/32.8. Author failure analysis includes hallucinated objects and ambiguous stopping. DEDUCTION: frozen high-level reasoning is not a globally untrained pipeline. The official repository contains only a coming-soon README at the inspected commit.
limitations: No executable implementation released at inspected snapshot; references16-17 not reviewed.

title: Schrodinger's Navigator: Imagining an Ensemble of Futures for Zero-Shot Object Navigation
review_scope: Methods, experiments and stated limitations on listed pages; figure-only pages are not counted as visually inspected unless separately recorded.
review: AUTHOR METHOD: FlashWorld imagines left/right/overhead virtual views, aligns depth and combines source-tagged observed/imagined primitives into semantic/exploration/risk maps. These trajectories are complementary cameras, not independent posterior world samples. Imagined semantic cues receive a fixed discount; observations and futures remain separately stored. PAPER EXPERIMENT: Increasing imagination weight can hurt; author limitations deny formal safety guarantees. HM3D uses ShortestPathFollower. Table 1's ImagineNav++ comparator equals its oracle-real-view row; protocol/version clarification is needed. Physical evidence is 30 trials per condition in three rooms. DEDUCTION: source tagging, discounts and multiview imagination alone are not new; calibrated decision risk and actual low-level execution remain distinct questions.
limitations: No official executable code located; videos not reviewed; qualitative image-only pages not inspected.

title: Dream to Recall: Imagination-Guided Experience Retrieval for Memory-Persistent Vision-and-Language Navigation
venue_or_status: TPAMI accepted 15 March 2026 per official repository
review_scope: Methods, experiments and stated limitations on listed pages; figure-only pages are not counted as visually inspected unless separately recorded.
review: AUTHOR METHOD: A language-conditioned world model queries separate observation/behavior memories; DUET gains a history encoder and three-way action fusion. Persistent graphs permit inter-episode retrieval. PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table V controls instruction/state/random/full retrieval; oracle retrieval remains much stronger. §V.E identifies similar-goal confusion, premature imagination and equal treatment of failed/successful history. Continuous transfer improves success but loses path fidelity versus episodic DUET. INSPECTED CODE: history matching ranks cumulative compatibility products rather than the described prefix-minimum criterion; inference termination threshold differs from the supplement. Teacher paths in the inspected retrieval helper only calculate diagnostics. DEDUCTION: generic future-guided retrieval is established, and confidence-aware retrieval is explicitly suggested future work; a new proposal needs a sharper mechanism/test.
limitations: No code execution; full training/loss pipeline not audited; cited theorem derivations not independently certified.

title: Long-Horizon Model-Based Offline Reinforcement Learning Without Explicit Conservatism
review_scope: Methods, experiments and stated limitations on listed pages; figure-only pages are not counted as visually inspected unless separately recorded.
review: AUTHOR METHOD: A history-dependent Bayesian offline-RL policy learns across an ensemble of dynamics models; rollouts stop using in-dataset uncertainty quantiles. Long horizons reduce bootstrap reliance while layer normalization controls predicted increments. PAPER EXPERIMENT: D4RL/NeoRL studies support dataset-dependent benefits; parameters are tuned using true-environment performance and narrow-coverage tasks remain difficult. DEDUCTION: uncertainty-triggered rollout truncation and history-based adaptation are established beyond VLN. Eq 4 bounds prediction magnitudes, not closeness to the true trajectory by itself. No probability-calibration or instruction-following guarantee follows. This is a scoped main-paper comparison, not a review of its extensive supplementary proofs or implementation.
limitations: Full supplement pp10-50 and implementation not reviewed; no reproduction.

title: Confidence Calibration in Vision-Language-Action Models
venue_or_status: TMLR, October 2026, as stated in final manuscript
review_scope: Only the explicitly listed text sections and source files were reviewed; no benchmark execution.
review: AUTHOR METHOD: Mean selected-token probabilities estimate eventual episode success; instruction-paraphrase ensembles and action-wise Platt scaling recalibrate the score. PAPER EXPERIMENT: Fine-tuned token-based VLAs in LIBERO support calibration improvements, not physical safety. Temporal alignment uses realized episode length retrospectively; the proposed progress-aware intervention is qualitative and requires an online progress estimator. Rephrased actions are discarded: original instructions control execution. INSPECTED CODE: each dimension is fitted separately against the same terminal label; the experiment explicitly averages outputs despite a product constructor default. DEDUCTION: neither paraphrase-based confidence nor generic progress-conditioned monitoring is new. Separate risk discrimination, calibration and intervention utility under policy/scene shift.
limitations: Supplement pp.22-34 not reviewed; no notebook execution or raw rollout inspection; OpenReview verification page inaccessible.

title: ReliableNav: Uncertainty-Aware Zero-Shot Vision-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments

review: AUTHOR ABSTRACT: Atomic action reasoning and a reliability-check map address semantic and sampling uncertainty. INSPECTED CODE: clustered same-class landmark instances receive numbered image masks and trigger another subgoal query; geometry rejects nonnavigable choices. This is explicit disambiguation/replanning, not a verified probability-calibration mechanism. The released configuration defaults to replayed action/LLM logs for 100 R2R-CE episodes. title: Uncertainty-Calibrated Safety Gating for Vision-Language-Action Manipulation Under Domain Shift: Reliability Gains and Intervention-Efficiency Trade-Offs
reviewed_pdf_pages: HTML sections 3.2,4.1-4.3,5.3,6.1-6.4,9 and Tables2-7; partial text review
review_scope: Only the explicitly listed text sections and source files were reviewed; no benchmark execution.
review: AUTHOR METHOD: A calibrated failure-risk score selects normal control, pause/reobserve or a MoveIt fallback. PAPER EXPERIMENT: Two simulated manipulation tasks under structured visual shifts show an intervention-efficiency tradeoff; the more aggressive uncalibrated baseline has stronger raw success/collision results. Threshold sweeps are retrospective, not rerun policies; most interventions use fallback, and residual contacts occur during pause/fallback. The authors explicitly deny a formal safety guarantee. DEDUCTION: a calibrated three-way gate alone is not a new mechanism; equal intervention budgets and closed-loop testing are essential. No released executable implementation or underlying logs were inspected.
limitations: Partial HTML review; access intermittent; data offered on request; no code or raw-data audit.
